themes.label: Pact for the Future and AI at UN
themes.definition: The UN, via the Pact for the Future, as the venue for addressing AI, whether praised as opening the AI conversation or criticized for its process.
themes.inclusion: Passages linking AI to the Pact for the Future or asserting that AI rules must be agreed universally within the UN.
themes.exclusion: General UN reform passages without AI content.
themes.boundary_cases: Criticism of the Pact's drafting counts here when tied to AI legal frameworks.

examples.quote: We also opened a conversation about the critically important issue of how to make artificial intelligence a force for good.
Those issues touch upon the future of all humankind and must be considered on a universal basis, without discrimination or aspirations to achieve unilateral benefits.

themes.label: Objection to Western narrow AI formats
themes.definition: Objection that Western states create narrow formats outside the UN to set AI legal frameworks, undermining universal and equal participation.
themes.inclusion: Passages accusing specific states or blocs of setting AI rules in exclusive or subordinate formats bypassing the UN.
themes.exclusion: General calls for inclusive governance without accusations of exclusive rule-making.
themes.boundary_cases: Also relevant to sovereignty/concentration; code here when the complaint is about governance venues.

examples.quote: in circumvention of the United Nations — to create subordinate, narrow formats to resolve crucial issues, such as control over the Internet or determination of legal frameworks to use artificial intelligence technologies

value.rationale: Both 2024 passages reference the Pact for the Future: Norway welcomes it for opening the AI-for-good conversation, while Russia contests Western-led, exclusive formats for setting AI legal frameworks and demands universal UN-based agreement.
